content.comment_body: I set up an NI1 memory bit using address VB249.0. To access this bit via Modbus/TCP, my other PLC communicates using address 125. Everything operates correctly, but I am unsure of the reasoning behind this behavior.

I'm also unsure why you repeatedly start new topics for the same issue. Additionally, creating threads in both the German-speaking and international sections, as well as duplicating in the German area, seems unnecessary. There is no memory address called VB249.0; what exists is a single bit, V249.0, and a byte, VB249.
This conversation is closed due to duplicate posting. The second thread under the subject 'Help?' appears in the section '[product_name] - Communication.' Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unsure about how memory bits are mapped when using Modbus/TCP, specifically how memory addresses correlate with Modbus addresses. Although functionality is as expected, the user is confused due to a lack of documentation and unclear explanations. Ambiguity or inaccuracies in memory address notation may further contribute to the confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a clear explanation and documentation showing how [product_name] memory addresses relate to Modbus addresses. They expect straightforward and understandable behavior for configuring memory with network protocols.
